newsitem.title: USA: Leach warns again of taking US bank reform too far.
newsitem.headline: Leach warns again of taking US bank reform too far.

text.p: U.S. House Banking Committee Chairman James Leach said there may be room for more investment by banks in non-bank activities than a bill he is proposing allows for, but warned of the danger of foreign companies buying up U.S. banks.

"Perhaps the 7.5 percent basket (of activities unrelated to banking) should be increased somewhat ... but it should be clear that the larger the allowed non-financial investments, the greater the attractiveness of banks to commercial enterprises and the greater (their) right ... to purchase banks," he said in a speech to a business group Wednesday.

"It is my belief that authorizing full-blown 'commerce and banking' would be like hanging a 'For Sale' sign in front of every bank in the country, particularly big banks..," Leach said in copies of his remarks issued Thursday.

Far from banks buying stakes in companies, he said, it was more likely the biggest U.S. and foreign companies would immediately begin gobbling up U.S banks, noting that Citicorp barely made it onto the last place in the top 20 major U.S. companies by market capitalization.

"... In embracing too extensively banking and commerce today, banks may jeopardize the likelihood of their own existence tomorrow. If commerce becomes fully integrated with banking, it is hard to believe a goodly number of American and foreign ... firms wouldn't immediately develop a dominant stakehold in all levels of American banking," he said, adding that this would not be in the U.S. national interest.
